title: fix(service-automation): engine.ts residual log-splice sweep — 13 foreign-text seams + the self-authored 14th, per-site #4632 verdicts (#6499)
body:
Closes #6499

The 13 residual `engine.ts` seams that still interpolated uncontrolled thrown text (a caught error's `.message`, or a foreign envelope field) into the log MESSAGE now log a single-line, consequence-stating message and hand the cause to the logger's structured slot (`describeThrownForLog`) — the exact shape PR #6498 merged for the three seams #6299 fixed in this same file. The separately-argued 14th site (`validateFlowExpressions`) is fixed alongside, on its own terms (section below). `evaluateCondition`'s multi-line **thrown** Error is deliberately untouched, per the issue's own scoping.

Mechanism (not re-derived; #6498's derivation now lives in `forgetSuspendedRun`'s catch and every new site comment points at it): `ObjectLogger.write()` emits one `[timestamp] [level]` head per call, so a cause carrying newlines turned ONE record into several physical lines of which only the first is greppable, and `serve`'s boot-quiet window drops the headless continuations outright on the stdout (warn) path.

## Per-site #4632 verdicts

Per #6299's lesson, the message fix is uniform but the level is not — each site was judged on its own consequence path. `pnpm check:durability-log-level` grades none of these (callee vocabulary / scan roots do not reach them), so **every** verdict below is pinned by a test in `engine-residual-log-cause.test.ts` (real bytes off a real `ObjectLogger`: level + stream + message-stays-one-line + cause-in-meta, against the family's byte-identical multi-line driver fixture).

| # | Site | Seam | Before | Verdict | Consequence rationale (one line) |
|---|------|------|--------|---------|-------------------------------|
| 1 | `persistSuspendedRun` | datasource (`store.save`) | `error` | **`error` (kept, no re-grade)** | #4460's raise stands: a durable pause silently kept in-memory is #4420's accident — data loss in waiting. |
| 2 | `listRuns` | datasource (`store.listHistory`) | `warn` | **`warn` (functional)** | Rows intact, nothing claimed-persisted failed to land; the Runs listing degrades to the ring buffer and the record now says the caller cannot tell a short list from a complete one. |
| 3 | `getRun` | datasource (`store.loadTerminal`) | `warn` | **`warn` (functional)** | Read degrades to `null`; the terminal row (if any) is intact. The #5186 invented-answer shape (null reads as "never ran") is stated out loud in the record; its remedy is propagation, a return-contract change outside this issue. |
| 4 | `recordLog` → `store.recordTerminal` | datasource, fire-and-forget `.catch()` | `warn` | **RAISED to `error` (durability)** | The write half of the run-history claim: a TERMINAL run's row failed to land while the run reads healthy everywhere; nothing retries it. After a restart, `inspectStrandedRequests` (#3456) reads "no suspension + no terminal row" as a STRANDED approval, and `releasePendingForTerminalRuns` (#4469) reads "no terminal row" as still-alive, so leftover pending approvals are never auto-released. #4632's question answers YES. |
| 5 | `releaseSuspension` | plugin (`NodeExecutor.onSuspensionReleased`) | `warn` | **`warn` (functional)** | The run continued; the leftover is whatever the node armed on entry (a misleading `sys_job` row, not a broken run). The operator's clean-up handle (correlation) stays in the message. |
| 6 | `unregisterTrigger` | plugin (`FlowTrigger.stop`) | `warn` | **`warn` (functional)** | Binding bookkeeping is dropped either way; worst case a subscription keeps firing into `execute()`'s own guards, visibly. |
| 7 | `activateFlowTrigger` | plugin (`FlowTrigger.start`) | `warn` | **`warn` (functional)** | "A trigger is not armed" is AGENTS.md's canonical `warn` example; the `kernel:bootstrapped` binding audit re-reports every unbound triggered flow. |
| 8 | `deactivateFlowTrigger` | plugin (`FlowTrigger.stop`) | `warn` | **`warn` (functional)** | Same consequence shape as site 6. |
| 9 | `resolveRunContext` | engine-internal (grants resolver throw) | `warn` | **`warn` (functional)** | Fail-safe, never fail-open: the run keeps the unresolved identity, is NOT elevated, and its own data-op refusals/strips are the visible symptom. |
| 10 | `expandDeclaredLookups` | engine-internal (expander throw) | `warn` | **`warn` (functional)** | Best-effort enrichment that must never break the flow it feeds; templates render the scalar id, visibly. |
| 11 | `refuseInvalidScreenInput` (visibility probe) | engine-internal (`evaluateCondition` throw over author metadata) | `warn` | **`warn` (functional)** | One field's `required` unenforced for one submission; the resume caller reads the outcome directly. Both spliced pieces were uncontrolled (the author's predicate AND the evaluator's deliberately multi-line throw) — both ride meta (`visibleWhen` + `error`). |
| 12 | `bubbleToParent` (envelope branch) | engine-internal (`AutomationResult.error` — carries driver text verbatim per #5912) | `warn` | **`warn` (functional)** | No false success recorded anywhere: the parent either failed terminally (recorded) or stays visibly parked and resumable; the child's completion is genuine. |
| 13 | `bubbleToParent` (catch branch) | engine-internal (parent resume threw) | `warn` | **`warn` (functional)** | Same envelope of consequences as site 12; the throw path's incremental fact is the child-to-parent linkage, which the record still names. |
| 14 | `validateFlowExpressions` (advisory pass) | self-authored `\n` (see below) | `warn` | **`warn` (kept, BY CONTRACT)** | #1928 defines the schema pass as advisory, logged-never-thrown, strictly additive to registration. |

Operator-visible: exactly one record moves stream and level (site 4, stdout/`WARN` to stderr/`ERROR`). Every reworded message keeps its original lead phrase (`run-history read failed`, `durable run lookup failed`, `Failed to bind flow`, `could not resolve grants`, …) so existing greps still match; anything keyed on the trailing `: [error text]` splice must read the structured `error` / `source` / `visibleWhen` fields instead. The changeset says the same.

## The 14th site, argued on its own terms

Sites 1–13 splice text **someone else** wrote into the message; `validateFlowExpressions`' advisory warn is the **opposite**: nothing threw and no envelope is involved — the old message itself authored a second physical line (`\n      source: \`…\``), and `issue.source` is the flow **author's** expression, whose line count is theirs (CEL is newline-tolerant; the pin test registers a two-line predicate cleanly to prove it). The downstream damage is identical — one record, several physical lines, only the first with a head — so the fix shape is the family's, but the reachability argument differs: this line needs no driver, no plugin, and no failure anywhere to shred; any advisory finding on any multi-line expression already does it. The message now stays one line (`issue.message` embeds at most identifier names, which cannot carry newlines in CEL), and the expression source rides the structured slot (`source`). Its level pin is contractual (#1928's logged-never-thrown), not a durability judgment — which is exactly why it must not be batched silently with the 13.

The fatal half of the same function (the `failures` array that becomes a **thrown** registration error) is untouched: it is `evaluateCondition`'s class, not a log record.

## Tests

- **New: `engine-residual-log-cause.test.ts`** (18 tests) — one pin per site: level + stream (both streams always captured), message stays one physical line and leaks no driver fact, the whole multi-line cause rides the structured slot (which, because JSON format spreads meta into the record, also proves the meta landed in the *right* argument slot — `warn(message, meta?)` second vs `error(message, error?, meta?)` third); explicit prototype-spy slot checks for the two `error` sites (Error slot deliberately empty, #5575); behaviour-unchanged asserts per seam (run still pauses / degrades to `[]` and `null` / child resume still succeeds / flow still registers). Sites 12–13 route only the parent-run id through a stubbed `resumeInternal` (envelope / throw) while the child's resume runs the real implementation — noted inline; there is no public route to a thrown parent resume today, which is what the catch exists for.
- **Updated (fixture triage, both pinned the old splice):** `suspension-release.test.ts` ("teardown that throws") and `suspended-run-store.test.ts` ("logs a failed durable write at ERROR") asserted the thrown message appears **in** the warn/error message — the exact defect. Both now assert the message keeps its controlled facts and the cause rides meta.
- **Reverse verification, direction predicted before running:** re-splicing site 2 (`listRuns`) turns exactly its two pins red (JSON: message gains the driver text / `record.error` vanishes; pretty: one record becomes 4 physical lines) — observed exactly that, 2 failed / 16 passed, then restored: 18/18 green.

Local runs (worktree, post-change):
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation test` → **70 files, 844 tests, all passed**.
- `tsc --noEmit` in the package (it has no `typecheck` script; ledgered DEBT=5): **3 errors, all pre-existing** in `nested-region-parity.test.ts` — below the ledgered count, my files contribute 0.
- `eslint` on the four touched files: clean. `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs`: OK; control-byte self-scan of touched files: clean.
- `node scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` and `check-startup-registry-verdict.mjs`: green (the former still cannot see these seams — that is why the levels are test-pinned).

## Full-file residual sweep (the honesty requirement)

#6299 closed with "this file is now clean" and was wrong; here is what **actually remains** in `engine.ts` after this PR that interpolates text the engine does not fully control into a log MESSAGE — none of it fixed here, per the issue's own scope pin ("fix only the listed ones, report the extras"):

1. **`:1732` (`activateFlowTrigger`'s trigger callback), the one clear same-class site**: `Trigger-fired run of flow '…' failed: ${result.error ?? 'unknown error'}` at `logger.error` — splices the `AutomationResult.error` envelope field, which carries a failing node's / driver's text verbatim (#5912): the identical class as site 12, on the fired-run path instead of the subflow path. It is **not** on #6499's list of 13, so it is reported, not fixed.
2. **Weaker tail — author-metadata / caller-supplied *names* (not thrown text, not envelopes), spliced as identifiers:** `:2719` (record id from user data, re-entrancy guard), `:3365` (engine-internal variable names from the caller's resume signal), `:3598` (screen-input refusal summary — embeds user-submitted *keys* via `Unknown screen field "…"`), `:4209` (node type names from flow metadata), `:4899` (computed branch label, potentially record-derived, + edge labels). Each can in principle carry a newline (none is schema-constrained to reject one); none is a thrown-text or envelope splice, which is the class #6499 names.
3. **Controlled-text interpolations, listed for completeness, not defects of this class:** `:2191`/`:2195` (ADR-0087 conversion notices — in-repo authored messages), and the many flowName / engine-minted runId / enum-reason interpolations.
4. **Deliberate non-log multi-line composers, out of scope by the issue's own text:** `evaluateCondition` and `validateFlowExpressions`' fatal `failures` array — both build **thrown** messages, whose text then lands in exactly the envelopes item 1 and site 12 splice(d).

So the honest closing claim is narrower than #6299's: after this PR, **no site on #6499's list splices uncontrolled text into a log message; one known same-class site (`:1732`) and a tail of name-shaped splices remain, enumerated above** for the PM to triage.
